target.title: fix(codex): cap sandbox file copy reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

- **Affected surface / workflow:** Codex sandbox exec-server filesystem `fs/copy` when copying a sandbox file through the app-server fs bridge.
- **Root cause, in product terms:** `fs/readFile` already stats the sandbox path and rejects files above the 512 MiB exec-server read limit before calling `fsBridge.readFile`. The file branch of `copySandboxPath()` also reads the entire source file into memory, but it called `fsBridge.readFile({ filePath: params.sourcePath })` directly after `stat` without applying the same size check.
- **Why it matters / User impact:** Copying an oversized sandbox file could make the app-server buffer that file all at once, bypassing the existing memory guard that direct reads use.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Fix classification:** Minimal root-cause fix.
- **Complete shipped solution:** Reuses a single `assertSandboxFileReadWithinLimit()` guard from both `fs/readFile` and the file-copy path. Recursive directory copies now apply the same per-file cap when they recurse into file leaves.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** The unsafe buffering boundary was immediately before `copySandboxPath()` reads a source file into memory; the patch enforces the existing read-file contract at that boundary.
- **Key design boundary / source of truth:** Keeps `CODEX_SANDBOX_EXEC_SERVER_MAX_READ_FILE_BYTES` as the single source of truth for sandbox exec-server in-memory file reads.
- **Non-goals / what did not change:** Does not change the 512 MiB limit, introduce streaming copy semantics, alter directory traversal/listing behavior, or broaden sandbox policy permissions.
- **Compatibility, merge-risk, or maintainer-decision notes:** Oversized `fs/copy` file operations now fail with the same error used by oversized `fs/readFile`. Normal file copies and recursive directory copies are preserved.
- **Risk labels considered:** `merge-risk:low`, `area:codex`, `area:sandbox`.
- **Risk explanation:** The diff is limited to the Codex sandbox exec-server filesystem handler plus a focused regression test. It reuses an existing limit and error message instead of introducing a new behavior surface.
- **Why acceptable:** The behavior change only rejects files that already exceed the exec-server's established in-memory read cap.

## User Impact

- **Users/operators/developers can now:** Rely on the Codex sandbox exec-server copy path to respect the same in-memory file size limit as direct reads.
- **Existing behavior preserved:** Allowed file copies still call `fsBridge.readFile` and `fsBridge.writeFile`; recursive copies still create directories and copy supported file leaves.
- **What was not tested or remains unavailable:** I did not make the production handler read a real >512 MiB payload into memory. Instead, the live proof uses a sparse 536,870,913-byte sandbox file and confirms the production WebSocket `fs/copy` RPC rejects from `stat` before `fsBridge.readFile` or `fsBridge.writeFile` is invoked.

## Evidence

- **Environment:** Windows Git Bash, Node v22.17.0, pnpm v11.2.2. `pnpm exec` reported the repository's Node engine warning (`wanted >=22.19.0 <23 || >=23.11.0`) before running the focused test/proof.
- **Commands run after this patch:**
  - `git fetch origin main` followed by inspection of `origin/main:extensions/codex/src/app-server/sandbox-exec-server/filesystem.ts`; latest checked `origin/main` still had the direct `fsBridge.readFile({ filePath: params.sourcePath })` copy path and no `assertSandboxFileReadWithinLimit(sourceStat)` guard.
  - Open-PR duplicate checks: `copySandboxPath`, `CODEX_SANDBOX_EXEC_SERVER_MAX_READ_FILE_BYTES`, and the oversized-read error text each returned 0 open PRs; the `sandbox-exec-server/filesystem` search results were checked with `gh pr diff <pr> --name-only`, and none changed `extensions/codex/src/app-server/sandbox-exec-server/filesystem.ts` or `extensions/codex/src/app-server/sandbox-exec-server.fs.test.ts`.
  - `pnpm exec node --import tsx <temporary proof harness>` from the repository root. The harness dynamically imported the production Codex sandbox exec-server, started its local WebSocket JSON-RPC server, created a sparse 536,870,913-byte sandbox file, sent `fs/copy`, and recorded fs bridge call counters.
  - `pnpm exec vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-codex-app-server-tools.config.ts --reporter=verbose extensions/codex/src/app-server/sandbox-exec-server.fs.test.ts`.
  - `git diff --check HEAD~1..HEAD`.
- **Key results / observations:** Real behavior proof passed, focused Vitest passed, and whitespace checks passed.
  - Real behavior proof transcript, redacted for host temp paths:
    ```text
    Codex sandbox fs/copy oversized-file live proof
    repo_head=7ce35f8e9e2c96ffce4bd4d39482af62b48ab2d7
    source_sandbox_path=/workspace/huge.bin
    source_size_bytes=536870913
    destination_sandbox_path=/workspace/huge-copy.bin
    host_temp_root=<redacted>
    stat_calls=["/workspace/huge.bin"]
    rpc_error="file is too large to read through Codex sandbox exec-server: 536870913 bytes"
    fsBridge.readFile_calls=0
    fsBridge.writeFile_calls=0
    destination_created=false
    proof_result=PASS
    ```
  - Focused Vitest: 1 test file passed, 15 tests passed. The new regression `rejects oversized file copies before buffering through the fs bridge` passed and verifies `readFile`/`writeFile` are not called for an oversized file-copy source.
  - `git diff --check HEAD~1..HEAD` exited 0.
- **Review findings addressed, if any:** RF-001, RF-002, RF-004, and RF-005 are addressed by the real WebSocket `fs/copy` proof transcript above. RF-003 is called out in the compatibility/risk notes: oversized `fs/copy` now intentionally fails with the established in-memory read cap instead of buffering.
- **Regression guardrail:** The sandbox filesystem test suite now covers direct oversized reads and oversized copies side by side, so future changes that reintroduce an unguarded copy read will fail the focused test.
- **Patch quality notes:** Two production call sites share the same helper; no unrelated files, lockfiles, or generated artifacts are included.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High for this focused memory-guard regression now that the production WebSocket `fs/copy` path has live proof showing the oversized sparse file is rejected before buffering.
